A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Perception Magnifier (PM) work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete supplementary materials are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations and qualitative examples, including supplementary Shikra experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds M3ID comparisons, hyperparameter sensitivity results and detailed POPE scores.

M1.justification: PM retains multi-layer attention aggregation, iterative token masking, heatmap post-processing and image resampling at each decoding step. Algorithm 1 documents the existing refinement procedure. Selective magnification and speculative decoding are proposed future directions, not implemented changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MME perception and cognition, POPE over AOKVQA/GQA/COCO, and both LLaVA-Bench components. The new POPE split table disaggregates existing coverage; the hyperparameter sweep adds no dataset or task scenario. The illustrative CLEVR-style failure case is retained.

E2.justification: M3ID, whose source was already cited in v1, becomes an evaluated comparator in the LLaVA benchmark tables and supplementary Shikra comparison. Other substantive comparator families remain; the prompting rows Crop and Crop & Resize are relabeled Masking and ViCrop with retained scores.

E3.justification: v3 adds an MME sensitivity protocol varying alpha across 7, 10 and 15 and beta from 0 through the plotted 1.0+ setting. Existing model configurations, default PM hyperparameters, beam size and GPT-4o evaluation procedures remain unchanged. Newly disclosed computing infrastructure does not establish a changed experimental setting.

E4.justification: The new Figure 4 tests sensitivity to magnification strength and the iterative-refinement stopping threshold. Existing component, perception-map and image-prompting ablations are retained, as are the qualitative successes and failure examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or empirical uncertainty estimates. The new hyperparameter curves show setting-dependent scores, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: v3 adds M3ID results, nine-way POPE breakdowns and hyperparameter curves. In Table 1, VCD's reported LLaVA MME perception total changes from 586.67 to 608.33 and POPE average from 83.99 to 84.40, without an explained setting change. Existing PM benchmark and ablation scores remain unchanged, including 683.33 MME perception and 86.70 POPE average.

T1.justification: The substantive attention aggregation, heatmap normalization and inverse-resampling mathematics are retained. Algorithm 1 restates the existing iterative-refinement formulation, while the supplementary relative-score formula restates the previously described metric. No theorem, proof or substantive formal assumption is added.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces its assertion that previous approaches impair language reasoning with a limitation in capturing fine-grained visual details. PM's central contribution claims—adaptive magnification, attention grounding and hallucination mitigation while preserving reasoning—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands practical limitations by explicitly identifying incompatibility with KV caching and the cost of applying PM throughout long generations. It adds concrete future remedies for efficiency and shape distortion, plus interpretations of hyperparameter interactions and GQA difficulty. The new POPE discussion overstates performance across all splits despite exceptions in Table 5.

D1.justification: The new Computing Infrastructure section specifies the RTX 3090 GPU, CPU, operating system, CUDA, PyTorch and Transformers versions. Conversely, v3 removes v1's code-availability statement and repository link. This establishes reduced access information in the PDF, not that the repository became unavailable.

R1.justification: v3 trims general LLM and pretraining background references and adds Seeing More with Less and ONLY. It also emphasizes ViCrop's additional visual tokens and computation. The central positioning against contrastive decoding, image prompting and cropping remains intact.

P1.justification: Related work, method explanations and experimental discussion are extensively condensed and rewritten. General VLM background is folded into the hallucination discussion, cognition analysis and GPT evaluation details move to the supplement, and separate analyses are consolidated under ablations. Section hierarchy and citation style also change throughout.

P2.justification: Displays are extensively reorganized: cognition totals enter Table 1 while the detailed table moves to the supplement, and two ablation tables merge into Table 4. v3 adds Algorithm 1, the POPE breakdown table and a hyperparameter plot, expands Figure 3 with raw heatmaps, and changes typography, table styling and page layout throughout.

improvement.justification: The added comparator, sensitivity analysis, detailed POPE scores and computing information make the retained findings easier to assess. Explicit discussion of KV-caching limitations improves practical transparency. These gains are tempered by removal of the code link and the unsupported all-splits POPE claim: Table 5 reports GQA-Popular accuracy of 84.37 for PM versus 85.27 for VDD. Overall, the improvement is useful but limited.
